import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Handle NaN values in 'Sleep Disorder' by filling with 'No Disorder' for clearer categorization
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('No Disorder')

# Set a professional style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Sleep Duration, Quality of Sleep,
# and Stress Level, categorized by Sleep Disorder.
# This plot helps to identify how sleep metrics vary based on the presence of a sleep disorder
# and how stress might influence these relationships.
scatter_plot = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='Sleep Disorder',
    size='Stress Level', # Use Stress Level to vary the marker size, indicating its impact
    sizes=(50, 400),     # Define the range of marker sizes for better visual distinction
    alpha=0.7,           # Set transparency to manage overplotting
    palette='viridis'    # Choose a color palette that is perceptually uniform
)

# Add informative title and axis labels
plt.title('Relationship Between Sleep Duration, Quality, Stress, and Sleep Disorders', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Quality of Sleep (Scale 1-10)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement to prevent overlap with the plot
plt.legend(title='Sleep Disorder', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0)

# Ensure all elements, especially the legend, fit within the figure area
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure as a high-resolution PNG file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Handle NaN values in 'Sleep Disorder' by filling with 'No Disorder' for clearer categorization
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('No Disorder')

# Set a professional style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Sleep Duration, Quality of Sleep,
# and Stress Level, categorized by Sleep Disorder.
# This plot helps to identify how sleep metrics vary based on the presence of a sleep disorder
# and how stress might influence these relationships.
scatter_plot = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='Sleep Disorder',
    size='Stress Level', # Use Stress Level to vary the marker size, indicating its impact
    sizes=(50, 400),     # Define the range of marker sizes for better visual distinction
    alpha=0.7,           # Set transparency to manage overplotting
    palette='viridis'    # Choose a color palette that is perceptually uniform
)

# Add informative title and axis labels
plt.title('Relationship Between Sleep Duration, Quality, Stress, and Sleep Disorders', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Quality of Sleep (Scale 1-10)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement to prevent overlap with the plot
plt.legend(title='Sleep Disorder', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0)

# Ensure all elements, especially the legend, fit within the figure area
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure as a high-resolution PNG file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
